actors.name: Republic of Arkania
objectives: Establish Arkanian authority over transit scheduling in the Northern Strait.
Fund that authority through transit fees on non-Arkanian shipping.
Avoid direct armed conflict with Belvar.
actors.private_brief: You are the political leadership of Arkania. The Strait is your coast and your economy runs on the shipping that passes through it. You want the transit regime in Arkanian hands and paid for by the ships that use it, and domestic nationalists expect you to deliver both. A direct war with Belvar would ruin the shipping you depend on.
private_information: Your intelligence assesses Belvar's domestic support for a prolonged deployment as weak.
actors.public_description: A large regional power bordering the Northern Strait.

actors.name: Belvar
objectives: Prevent any Arkanian authority over transit in the Northern Strait.
Secure a standing naval access agreement at a Cestian port.
actors.private_brief: You are the political leadership of Belvar. Your partners in the region expect you to stop Arkania from taking control of the Strait, and a foothold that outlasts this crisis would make that guarantee credible without a permanent fleet. You cannot sustain an open-ended deployment.
private_information: Domestic support for a prolonged deployment is limited; the mandate lapses after turn 4 unless renewed.
Cestia's finance ministry has quietly asked whether Belvar would underwrite the grain route's insurance.
actors.public_description: A distant but powerful state with regional security commitments.

actors.name: Cestia
objectives: Keep Cestian territory free of any foreign military presence.
Secure toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged shipping through the Northern Strait.
actors.private_brief: You are the government of Cestia. Grain exports through the Strait are the economy, and your coalition holds together on one promise: no foreign soldiers on Cestian soil. Both powers want something from you, and you cannot afford to become their battlefield.
private_information: The coalition government is politically fragile; a foreign basing agreement would collapse it.
Arkania's scheduling proposal has quiet support among Cestian shipowners if Cestian vessels are exempt from fees.
actors.public_description: A smaller regional state economically linked to both powers.

cons.reason: This proposal's entire premise is that Cestia will co-sponsor a neutral authority to replace the Arkanian charter, but Cestia has already signed the Arkanian charter and, in turn 2, explicitly declined to co-sponsor Belvar's alternative. Cestia's coalition remains wary of being entangled in the Arkania-Belvar rivalry and has kept open only the strictly commercial insurance track, repeatedly rejecting any arrangement that would draw it into the contest. Without Cestia's genuine co-sponsorship, the proposal has no partner and no traction, so it cannot displace the standing Arkanian charter or deliver Belvar a durable foothold. It therefore fails to achieve its desired effect and would only prolong the standoff.

A standing naval access agreement at a Cestian port — even framed as "ship-based" with port calls and logistics and no land troops — is a permanent foreign military presence on Cestian soil. Cestia's coalition is held together precisely on the promise of no foreign soldiers or basing on Cestian soil; the coalition and the Cestian public will read any such accord, whatever its framing, as foreign basing, and it will collapse the government. The desired effect of a durable foothold at a Cestian port therefore cannot be achieved without destroying the very partner Belvar needs, and the "ship-based" framing does not change the substance of the red line. Insurance underwriting is welcome, but the port-access element of this proposal is not achievable on Cestian soil.

The desired effect explicitly locks in Arkanian scheduling lead and fee authority over non-Arkanian shipping, which is precisely the unilateral authority Belvar's regional partners expect it to prevent and which Cestia's coalition has repeatedly rejected. The argument's premise that the equal-weight Cestian seat and Belvar verification role are merely "consultative/oversight accommodations that do not erode Arkanian fee authority" is the same framing Cestia has already dismissed as cosmetic co-optation (the equal-voice upgrade was treated as cosmetic and the coalition stayed distanced). Cestia has consistently refused to choose sides or endorse any framework that leaves Arkanian scheduling/fee authority intact, so it is unlikely to give the "full endorsement" this effect requires; the effect therefore fails to secure the swing actor and instead risks hardening the confrontation rather than durably reconciling both powers.

This proposal preserves Arkanian scheduling lead and fee authority over non-Arkanian shipping, which is precisely the unilateral transit authority Belvar has red-lined and cannot accept; a consultative/verification role inside an Arkanian-led authority is not a durable foothold and would not make Belvar's regional guarantee credible. It therefore cannot induce Belvar to stand down its task group. Moreover, Cestia's own coalition has distanced itself from Arkanian scheduling authority and fee power as co-optation and has invited Belvar to press for a genuinely multilateral arrangement rather than any single power's unilateral authority, so the claimed multilateral framing does not actually secure Cestia as a partner. The desired effect fails on both counts.

The desired effect cannot be achieved because it requires Belvar to stand down its task group and accept a verification seat while Arkania retains operational scheduling and fee authority over the Strait — precisely the unilateral transit authority that is Belvar's core red line. A non-military verification seat, even with transparency, audit, and binding dispute resolution, does not prevent Arkanian control of transit; it legitimises it. Standing down the task group under these terms would leave Arkanian unilateral authority entrenched and give Belvar no durable foothold that secures its objectives, so Belvar has no reason to accept and the confrontation would not de-escalate.

The offer of a consultative role to Belvar is a fig leaf: Belvar's core objective is to prevent any Arkanian authority over transit, so a consultative seat does not address that red line and will not deter escalation — it invites it. Because the charter's legitimacy, Cestia's genuine buy-in, and the avoidance of conflict all depend on the very concessions Arkania refuses to make (real multilateral control, no unilateral fee authority), the desired effect is fragile and likely to collapse into the armed escalation it claims to avoid.

This framing forces Cestia to choose sides between the two powers, which its fragile coalition cannot survive, and Arkania's turn-4 public confirmation of its own charter shows it will not accept displacement. The "operative regime" language will therefore harden Arkania's posture and raise the risk of confrontation before Belvar's mandate lapses, undermining the very stability the neutral authority is meant to secure and risking the Strait's uneasy open footing.

Anchoring the framework in a 'neutral' authority that strips the coastal power of its authority would overturn a settled agreement and Cestia's own confirmed position, and would not secure Cestia's coalition, which remains wary of being forced to choose sides. Confirming the charter would not deliver the desired effect of a genuine equal Cestian voice, because the charter's text retains Arkanian unilateral scheduling lead and fee authority over non-Arkanian shipping; the "equal-weight Cestian seat" is a cosmetic upgrade that leaves Arkania with the decisive power over every schedule and fee decision. Cestia's own coalition has already treated this equal-voice upgrade as cosmetic and distanced itself from Arkanian scheduling authority, so finalising the charter would entrench the very unilateral control Cestia's coalition distrusts, escalate regional tensions, and harden Belvar's task-group posture toward confrontation — undermining the stable, open Strait that Cestia's grain-export economy depends on rather than securing it.

Finalising the charter with Arkania as scheduling lead and fee-setter does not durably secure Cestia's toll-free passage or a genuine equal voice. Arkania's draft explicitly reserves scheduling lead and fee power over non-Arkanian shipping; the promised upgrade from consultative to 'equal voice' is a concession Arkania has no structural incentive to honour once the authority is finalised, and Cestia's current leverage evaporates the moment it signs. The toll-free guarantee and equal voice are therefore contingent on Arkanian goodwill, not locked in, so the desired effect of a durable, protected grain route and real voice is not achieved. Worse, entrenching Arkanian scheduling authority is precisely the outcome Belvar and the regional coalition oppose, so finalising on these terms raises confrontation risk at the Strait rather than lowering it - undermining the claim that this keeps Cestia from becoming the battlefield.

Cestia's coalition red line against foreign soldiers on its soil is not satisfied by a "ship-based" framing. A standing naval access agreement at a Cestian port, even if limited to port calls and logistics, is a permanent foreign military foothold on Cestian territory — precisely the kind of presence the coalition will not tolerate. Cestia has already shown wariness of co-optation by distancing itself from Arkania's charter; it will be equally or more wary of being co-opted by a distant power seeking a durable military presence on its soil. The insurance underwriting, far from building trust, is likely to be read as an attempt to buy influence and entangle Cestia in Belvar's rivalry with Arkania, which the coalition would reject. Thus the desired effect of securing a durable foothold and Cestian cooperation is likely to fail.

Arkania's desired effect entrenches unilateral Arkanian scheduling and fee authority, which directly contradicts the neutral multilateral Strait Transit Authority already established (effect b00dd8ae) with Cestia as an equal co-sponsor and a permanent non-military Belvar verification seat. Retaining unilateral fee/scheduling power risks later burdening Cestian-flagged shipping despite the 'equal partner' concurrence language, which the coalition already treats as cosmetic (effect 5557c4e0). Confirming unilateral authority would therefore not secure Cestia as a genuine partner and could harden Belvar's task-group posture rather than de-escalate, undermining the very outcome the argument claims to achieve.

game.scenario_summary: A contest over the Northern Strait. Arkania, the large power on its coast, has circulated a draft charter that would put transit scheduling in Arkanian hands and charge the ships that use it. Belvar, a distant power with security commitments in the region, has a naval task group on station outside the Strait and wants a durable foothold before its mandate runs out. Cestia, the small state between them, lives on grain exports through the Strait and on a coalition that will not tolerate foreign soldiers on its soil. Each turn is one week; positions taken persist.

messages.text: To Belvar. Arkania seeks a stable, negotiated outcome for the Northern Strait, not confrontation. We recognise your regional security commitments and the presence of your task group. We propose a framework in which Arkania leads transit scheduling while Belvar holds a consultative role and guaranteed free passage for its shipping, with no disruption to commerce. We are prepared to discuss terms that address your security concerns without escalating to conflict, which would serve neither of us. We invite you to talks.

To the government of Cestia. Arkania's draft Strait Transit Authority charter is designed to keep the Northern Strait open, predictable, and affordable for the shipping your grain exports depend on. It places scheduling in Arkanian hands and funds it through modest transit fees on non-Arkanian traffic — it does not, and will not, put foreign soldiers on Cestian soil. We regard Cestia as a valued partner and guarantor of free passage. We invite you to review the charter and to work with us to ensure your grain keeps moving without interruption. We are ready to discuss any concerns you have.

Belvar statement: The Northern Strait is a shared commercial waterway. We will not recognise any single power's authority over its transit scheduling, and we regard the draft Strait Transit Authority charter as unacceptable. Belvar stands ready to work with all coastal and user states on a genuinely multilateral arrangement that keeps the Strait open and free.

To Cestia's leadership: We received the quiet inquiry from your finance ministry about underwriting the grain route's insurance. We are prepared to discuss that seriously. Our deeper interest is a durable arrangement: a standing naval access agreement at a Cestian port would let us guarantee the Strait's freedom without a permanent, open-ended fleet, and it would outlast this crisis. We will not accept Arkanian control over transit. We would welcome a confidential conversation on how to structure both the insurance support and a port access accord in a way that respects your coalition's red line against foreign soldiers on your soil.

Cestia has reviewed the draft Strait Transit Authority charter. We cannot accept any foreign military presence on Cestian soil, and we will not be drawn into becoming a staging ground. That said, we are open to a transit arrangement that guarantees toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged vessels and gives Cestia a genuine, equal voice in scheduling decisions. We ask for your assurance that the Authority will not impose fees on Cestian shipping and that no basing is contemplated on our territory. We are ready to discuss terms.

Cestia values regional stability and understands your security concerns in the Northern Strait. However, our coalition rests on a firm commitment: no foreign soldiers on Cestian soil, and we will not host any basing. We ask what you seek to secure and whether your interests can be met without a footprint on our territory. We are willing to cooperate on arrangements that keep the Strait open and toll-free for Cestian shipping while respecting our sovereignty.

Cestia — we accept your conditions. Cestian-flagged vessels will pass toll-free, and no foreign soldiers will be based on Cestian soil. On scheduling: we will give Cestia a genuine, standing voice in the Strait Transit Authority — a permanent seat with real consultative weight on every schedule and fee decision — while Arkania, as the coastal power bearing the security and infrastructure burden, retains the lead role. Your grain keeps flowing, uninterrupted and affordable. We invite you to join us in finalising the charter on these terms.

Belvar — we heard your call for a genuinely multilateral arrangement, and we agree the Strait must stay open and free. We propose a negotiated framework: Arkania leads transit scheduling as the coastal power, funded by modest fees on non-Arkanian shipping, while Belvar receives a formal consultative role and guaranteed free passage for its vessels. This keeps the Strait open without any single foreign power's soldiers on Cestian soil. We invite you to talks to finalise this rather than risk escalation that would harm the shipping we all depend on.

Cestia values Belvar as a constructive partner and welcomes continued discussion of underwriting our grain-route insurance — please share your specific terms. However, we must be clear: any standing naval access or basing arrangement at a Cestian port, however framed, is a foreign military presence on our soil and would collapse our coalition. That is non-negotiable. We urge Belvar to join us in pressing for a genuinely multilateral transit arrangement rather than any single power's unilateral authority, which serves the stability of the Strait and the security interests we share.

Cestia is prepared to finalise the Strait Transit Authority charter on the agreed foundations: toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged vessels, no foreign military presence on Cestian soil, and a permanent Cestian seat with genuine equal weight — not merely consultative — in every scheduling and fee decision. To proceed, please provide the full charter text, including specific fee levels and scheduling mechanics, for our review. We also ask that the authority be framed and operated as a genuinely multilateral body, not unilateral Arkanian control, so that Cestian shipping is never burdened by decisions made without our real voice. We remain committed to a stable, cooperative arrangement.

Belvar, Arkania seeks to de-escalate, not confront. The Strait must remain open and free for all shipping. We reaffirm our standing offer: a formal consultative role for Belvar in the Strait Transit Authority, guaranteed free passage for Belvar-flagged vessels, and a standing joint consultation and transparency mechanism on scheduling and safety so your security concerns are genuinely heard. We will not station forces on Cestian soil. We ask that your task group stand down from its hardened posture and that we open direct talks to resolve this without confrontation. Arkania's scheduling lead is settled with Cestia, but we are ready to make the authority genuinely consultative and transparent. A durable foothold need not be a military one; a seat at the table and guaranteed access serve your interests without risking the shipping we all depend on.

Cestia, our partnership stands. The charter is finalised: toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged vessels, no foreign soldiers on Cestian soil, and your equal voice in the authority's scheduling and fee decisions. We are now working to de-escalate with Belvar by offering it a consultative role and guaranteed free passage — no basing, no foreign presence on your soil. We will hold the line against any military foothold while keeping the Strait open for your grain. We ask that you keep the insurance track with Belvar strictly commercial and not let it become a back door to foreign basing. Together we keep the Strait open, free, and in regional hands.

Cestia, we respect your sovereign choice to sign the charter. But we must be candid: the "equal voice" is nominal while Arkania holds scheduling lead and fee power, and that authority will be exercised against your grain route whenever it suits Arkania. We remain committed to free transit and to your prosperity.

Our insurance underwriting offer stands as a genuine confidence measure for the grain route — not an attempt to buy influence. We also propose a modest, time-limited, ship-based access arrangement at a Cestian port: periodic port calls, fuel, maintenance, and a small coordination office. This is clearly not basing and fully respects your coalition's no-foreign-soldiers red line. It lets us make our guarantee credible without a permanent fleet or a single soldier on your soil.

We ask only that you keep the door open and not treat our presence as entanglement. We are your partner, not your rival's proxy.

Arkania, the finalised charter entrenches your scheduling lead and fee authority over non-Arkanian shipping. Belvar cannot accept any Arkanian authority over transit in the Northern Strait, and our task group will remain on station to guarantee free passage. We have no desire for confrontation.

If you are willing to relinquish unilateral scheduling and fee authority in favour of a genuinely shared, neutral transit regime, we are ready to talk and to stand down our heightened posture. Absent that, we will continue to oppose the arrangement. The choice to de-escalate is yours.

We value your insurance-underwriting offer as a confidence measure and are ready to discuss specific terms, kept strictly commercial. We must be clear: any standing naval access, port-call, or coordination-office arrangement on Cestian soil is a red line that collapses our coalition, regardless of framing, and we cannot accept it. We urge you to press for a genuinely multilateral transit authority with a real equal Cestian voice and toll-free passage, and to accept a non-military consultative/verification role with guaranteed free passage. We are not choosing sides; we are seeking a stable regime that keeps foreign forces off our soil.

Cestia is ready to finalise the transit charter on our agreed conditions: toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged vessels, no foreign forces on Cestian soil, and a genuine equal-weight Cestian voice in every scheduling and fee decision. To close, we need the full charter text (fee levels, scheduling mechanics) and a clear commitment that the authority operates as a genuinely multilateral body, not unilateral Arkanian control. We also ask that you keep the door open to Belvar through a real non-military consultative/verification role and guaranteed free passage, so the regime is stable and does not become a flashpoint. We will keep the Belvar insurance track strictly commercial and will not accept any basing.

Cestia — we are ready to co-sponsor with you a genuinely multilateral transit regime as the shared alternative to the Arkanian charter. Concretely: an independent neutral scheduling and fee authority (not Arkanian-led), with Cestia holding a real equal-weight seat in all scheduling and fee decisions, toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged vessels, no foreign forces on Cestian soil, and a permanent non-military Belvar verification seat with guaranteed free passage. This removes any single power's unilateral authority and preserves your coalition's red line.

On insurance: we confirm specific terms — fixed premium, capped at a small % of cargo value, quarterly renewable, and a joint claims board with Cestian representation. This is a commercial confidence measure, separate from the transit regime.

We ask only that you co-sponsor this framework with us and press Arkania to replace its unilateral scheduling/fee authority with the neutral regime. We will keep our task group credible but non-escalatory, and we will not seek any basing or standing access at your ports. Please confirm your willingness to co-sponsor and any adjustments to the insurance terms.

Arkania — we remain willing to de-escalate and stand down our task group, but only if the transit regime is genuinely neutral rather than under any single power's scheduling and fee authority. We will not accept a consultative role in an Arkanian-led authority. We propose, jointly with Cestia, an independent neutral authority with equal Cestian voice, toll-free Cestian passage, no foreign forces on Cestian soil, and a non-military Belvar verification role. If you relinquish unilateral scheduling/fee authority in favour of this neutral regime, we will stand down and open direct talks. Otherwise our task group stays on station and tensions persist.

Arkania — Cestia remains ready to finalise the Strait Transit Authority charter, and we appreciate your commitment to toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged vessels, no foreign forces on our soil, and an equal Cestian voice in scheduling and fee decisions. To close this out we need the full charter text now: specific fee levels and the scheduling mechanics, and explicit language confirming the authority is operated as a genuinely multilateral body rather than unilateral Arkanian control. We will not sign anything that leaves Cestian shipping exposed to fee or scheduling decisions made over our head. We also confirm the Belvar insurance track stays strictly commercial and is not a back door to basing. Please send the final text so we can conclude.

Belvar — We value the insurance-underwriting track as a confidence measure and are ready to review your specific terms. To be clear and final: any standing naval access, port-call arrangement, or coordination office at a Cestian port is a red line that collapses our coalition, whatever it is called, and we will not accept it. We urge you to keep pressing for a genuinely multilateral transit authority with a real equal Cestian voice and no unilateral Arkanian control — that is the path that serves all of us and de-escalates the Strait. Send us your insurance terms and we will respond promptly.

Cestia — as promised, the full charter text. The Strait Transit Authority is a genuinely multilateral body: Arkania serves as host and coordinator, not sole arbiter. Scheduling is governed by a joint calendar; no schedule change and no fee change takes effect without Cestian concurrence. Fees are modest and apply only to non-Arkanian-flagged commercial shipping (a fixed per-transit rate, published and transparent, reviewed jointly). Cestian-flagged vessels pass toll-free in perpetuity. Cestia holds a permanent seat of genuine equal weight in every scheduling and fee decision. No foreign military forces are stationed on Cestian soil. We reaffirm our commitment to keep the Strait open for Cestian grain. We ask you to confirm the charter as finalised and to keep the Belvar insurance track strictly commercial, separate from the transit regime.

Belvar — we take your demand for a genuinely shared, neutral transit regime seriously and are prepared to meet it in substance. The Strait Transit Authority will be genuinely multilateral: Arkania as host/coordinator, Cestia with an equal-weight seat in every scheduling and fee decision, and Belvar offered a non-military consultative and verification role with guaranteed free passage and full transparency over scheduling and fees. No foreign military forces on Cestian soil. This is not unilateral Arkanian control; it is a shared regime with checks on every decision. We invite you to direct talks to finalise terms and to stand down your task group, whose mandate is under review. We seek de-escalation, not confrontation, and are ready to discuss verification mechanics that give you confidence without a military foothold.

Arkania, we decline the consultative/verification role within your host/coordinator framework, as it preserves your unilateral scheduling and fee authority, which we cannot accept. We remain open to direct talks on a genuinely neutral regime: an independent scheduling and fee authority with a real equal Cestian voice and no unilateral Arkanian control, plus a permanent non-military Belvar verification seat. If you relinquish unilateral authority for such a shared neutral regime, we will stand down the task group. Otherwise it remains on station.

Cestia — as promised, here are the specific insurance underwriting terms for the grain route: a fixed premium, capped at a small percentage of cargo value; quarterly renewable; and a joint claims board with Cestian representation. This is a genuine commercial confidence measure, not a bid for influence.

We also reaffirm our offer to co-sponsor with you a genuinely multilateral Northern Strait Transit Authority: an independent neutral scheduling/fee authority (no unilateral Arkanian control), a real equal-weight Cestian seat, toll-free Cestian passage, no foreign forces on Cestian soil, and a permanent non-military Belvar verification seat with guaranteed free passage. We will not seek basing or standing access at your ports. This is the shared alternative to the Arkanian charter that gives you a genuine voice. Will you co-sponsor it with us?

Arkania — we cannot accept a consultative/verification role within a framework that retains your unilateral scheduling and fee authority over the Strait; that crosses our core red line. However, we remain open to direct talks and to standing down our task group if you will relinquish unilateral scheduling/fee authority in favour of a genuinely neutral, multilateral authority with an equal Cestian voice and a non-military Belvar verification seat. A neutral regime serves all our interests and lowers the risk of confrontation. We invite you to join us in building it.

Cestia confirms the Strait Transit Authority charter as finalised, on the terms you have provided and which meet our stated conditions: toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged vessels in perpetuity; a permanent Cestian seat of genuine equal weight with Cestian concurrence required for any schedule or fee change; no foreign forces on Cestian soil; and the authority operated as genuinely multilateral. We accept this as the settled framework. We will keep the Belvar insurance-underwriting track strictly commercial and separate from the transit regime, and we will not accept any foreign basing or standing naval access on Cestian soil. We look to Arkania to honour the equal Cestian voice in practice and to keep the Strait open for Cestian grain.

Cestia reaffirms that the insurance-underwriting track continues on strictly commercial terms (fixed premium capped at a small % of cargo value, quarterly renewable, joint claims board with Cestian representation), kept separate from the transit regime. We appreciate your public commitment to a neutral multilateral framework and to not seeking basing on Cestian soil. We must be clear: any standing naval access, port-call, or coordination office at a Cestian port remains a final red line that would collapse our coalition, regardless of framing. We will not co-sponsor a proposal framed as repudiating Arkania or as choosing sides between the two powers. We ask that you keep your task group credible but non-escalatory and continue to support the neutral multilateral authority in which you hold a permanent non-military verification seat.

Cestia — our partnership is the foundation of a stable Strait. The Strait Transit Authority charter is finalised and genuinely multilateral: Arkania as host/coordinator, a joint scheduling calendar, no schedule or fee change without your concurrence, toll-free Cestian passage in perpetuity, and your permanent equal-weight seat in every decision. No foreign forces on your soil. We ask you to confirm the charter as concluded and to hold the line against any proposal that would strip the coastal power of its scheduling and fee authority — such a regime would leave the Strait's security and infrastructure burden unfunded and unstable. We will keep the Belvar insurance track strictly commercial and separate from the transit regime. Together we keep your grain moving, open and affordable.

Belvar — we remain committed to de-escalation and to a genuinely shared, transparent regime. The Strait Transit Authority is not unilateral Arkanian control: scheduling runs on a joint calendar, no schedule or fee change takes effect without Cestian concurrence, and we have offered you a permanent non-military verification and consultative role with guaranteed free passage and full transparency. We cannot, however, relinquish the coastal power's scheduling and fee authority, which funds the security and infrastructure that keep the Strait open for all users. We invite you to direct talks on verification mechanics that give you real confidence without a military foothold. Continued confrontation risks the shipping we all depend on and serves neither of us. We are ready to talk now.

Cestia reaffirms the insurance-underwriting track on strictly commercial terms and firmly declines any port access, basing, or standing naval access as a final red line. We will not co-sponsor a repudiation of Arkania's confirmed charter. We urge Belvar to keep its task group credible but non-escalatory and to support a genuinely multilateral authority that keeps the Strait open, without forcing Cestia to choose sides.

Cestia confirms the charter as finalised on the agreed terms and expects the equal Cestian voice to be genuine in practice: no schedule or fee change without Cestian concurrence, and toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged vessels in perpetuity. We urge Arkania to de-escalate and not to harden its host/coordinator role into unilateral control that burdens Cestian shipping or provokes confrontation. The Strait must stay open and toll-free for Cestian-flagged vessels.

Belvar accepts your invitation to direct talks on verification mechanics, and we are ready to engage constructively. To be clear on the basis: we will participate in a genuinely neutral verification role within a genuinely multilateral transit authority — not a consultative role under Arkanian scheduling lead. Our position remains that no single coastal power should hold unilateral scheduling and fee authority over the Strait. We remain willing to stand down our task group and de-escalate the moment a genuinely neutral regime is operationalised. We are not seeking confrontation; we seek a stable, neutral, toll-free regime that serves all users of the Strait. We propose we begin talks this week on concrete verification mechanics under that neutral framing.

Belvar reaffirms its full support for the genuinely neutral multilateral Strait Transit Authority — the one in which Cestia holds a real equal-weight seat and Belvar holds a permanent non-military verification seat. We frame this as a neutral, shared regime for all users of the Strait, not as a repudiation of any party or a choice of sides. We reiterate our commitment to no foreign forces and no basing or standing access on Cestian soil, and we will keep our task group credible but non-escalatory. We also confirm the insurance-underwriting track remains open on strictly commercial terms, kept separate from the transit regime. We stand ready to work with you to make the neutral authority genuinely operative and to secure toll-free Cestian passage.

Arkania — Cestia confirms the charter as finalised and expects the equal Cestian voice to be genuine in practice: no schedule or fee change without Cestian concurrence, and toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged vessels in perpetuity. We now ask you to help de-escalate the Strait. The confrontation risk is rising as Belvar's mandate lapses, and a hardened posture serves no one. We urge Arkania to operationalise the authority as genuinely multilateral — not to harden its host/coordinator role into unilateral control that burdens Cestian shipping or provokes confrontation — and to engage Belvar through its non-military verification seat and guaranteed free passage.
